inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2-2026 10-Q (255.2M; XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding). Held FLAT: SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes are expensed in the flows. The Crinetics deal was all cash (cash on hand plus a $4.5B bridge/term-loan commitment), so there is no non-SBC issuance to model.
inputs.cash_note: Cash 6,143.5 + marketable securities current 1,708.9 + non-current 5,789.1 at 2026-06-30 (10-Q). Debt is the finance-lease liability only (112.2 at 2025-12-31; Vertex had no funded debt at 30-Jun). The Crinetics purchase and any term loan drawn to fund it sit in equity_bridge, which nets them correctly whether cash or debt paid.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (SEC XBRL): ShareBasedCompensation 685.9 cash-flow add-back + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 369.9 = 1,055.8. Vertex publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. H1-2026 runs at the same 9.0% of revenue (336.6 + 232.8).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock 2,017.4; H1-2026 806.4. Vertex is a funded repurchaser: diluted count fell 263.4M (FY2020) -> 255.2M (Q2-2026), so the flat count is paid for, not a convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~0.65 (defensive rare-disease pharma, low cyclicality) x 5.0% ERP = ~7.6%, rounded up to 8.0% for single-franchise concentration. Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in all three scenarios: franchise and pipeline risk is charged in the bear/bull driver paths and the weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating-lease cost (~$155M/yr) sits inside opex, so EBITDA is already after lease cost and the $2.05B operating-lease liability is NOT added to debt (one treatment). The small finance lease ($112M) is in total_debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table: profitable operating company; ~$12B revenue, ~33% net margin, no going-concern or pre-revenue features, so not a risked-NPV biotech template). First valuation of VRTX, no prior DCF or memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end). Owner FCF FY2025 = reported 3,193.8 - SBC incl withholding 1,055.8 - interest income 490.9 = 1,647.1 (13.7% margin). FY2025 is depressed by a 34% cash tax rate (1,566.7 cash taxes on ~4,664 pre-tax; Section 174 R&D capitalisation) and record 3.6% capex; H1-2026 actual owner FCF is 1,503 on 6,321 revenue (23.8%), with cash tax back to ~19% after the 2025 restoration of domestic R&D expensing. The projection starts from components, not the FY2025 margin. EBITDA margins are stated BEFORE SBC (GAAP EBITDA + SBC: FY2025 42.2%, H1-2026 44.8%); SBC path includes withholding taxes. CRINETICS: closed ~1-Sep-2026 (CRNX last traded 2026-08-31 at 84.95 vs the $85 cash offer; 15-12G filed 2026-09-11). Its revenue and its pre-2029 operating losses are folded into the FY2026-2029 growth and margin paths (management: accretive to non-GAAP operating income only in 2029); the ~$10B purchase net of ~$1.15B acquired cash is a bridge deduction. Acquired IPR&D (business-development spend Vertex expenses through opex) is left inside the margin as a recurring cost, except Crinetics, which is in the bridge. Terminal value: CF exclusivity (Trikafta ~2037, Alyftrek later) falls in years 11-14, so the base cap is 16x rather than the 20x compounder default, and the bear cap is 10x.
inputs.h1_double_count_note: The FY2026 projection is a full year discounted one period, but H1-2026 owner FCF (~1,500) is already inside the 30-Jun cash balance. The bridge removes it so it is not counted twice.

equity_bridge.note: ~$10.0B equity value ($85/share cash, incl. awards; 8-K 2026-07-07) less ~$1.15B Crinetics cash+investments acquired (1,205.8 at 2026-06-30 10-Q less ~2 months' burn at ~$110M/qtr). Closed ~2026-09-01 (CRNX 15-12G 2026-09-11). Funded by cash on hand + term loan/bridge ($4.5B committed); net effect on net cash is the same either way.

equity_bridge.item: H1-2026 owner FCF already in 30-Jun cash
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 reported FCF 2,307.9 - SBC 336.6 - withholding 232.8 - interest 235.4 = ~1,503; removed because the FY2026 projection counts the full year.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (16.5%) diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (8.2%). Equity is not the right anchor: Vertex returns cash through buybacks (~$2B/yr) and spends on acquired IPR&D (Alpine $4.4B in FY2024 drove a GAAP loss), so book value tracks neither earnings nor value. Revenue 3yr CAGR (10.4%) is selected; it matches management's 'sustained double-digit growth' framing and FY2026 guidance (+9-10%).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (FY2020 2,341.7 -> FY2022 3,117.3 -> FY2025 1,647.1) are far below reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC+withholding rose from 630 to 1,056 and interest income from 22 to 491 while FY2025 FCF was hit by a 34% cash tax rate (Section 174) and doubled capex. The negative owner-FCF CAGR is a FY2025 trough artefact (H1-2026 owner FCF annualises to ~3.0B), not a franchise in decline; it is not used for projection. FY2024 is distorted by the $4.4B Alpine IPR&D charge.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +10% = guidance $13.1-13.2B plus ~4 months of Palsonify. FY2027-28 ~9%: full-year Crinetics, povetacicept IgAN launch (PDUFA 30-Nov-2026), Casgevy and Journavx scaling, Alyftrek mix. Fades to 2.5% by FY2035 as CF matures and its exclusivity horizon approaches.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA. FY2026 42.5% (guided ~86% GM and $5.65-5.75B non-GAAP opex imply ~43% ex-SBC for standalone Vertex, less Crinetics Sep-Dec losses and deal costs). FY2027 dips to 41% on a full year of Crinetics opex (~$650M against ~$200M revenue). Recovers as Crinetics turns accretive in 2029 and non-CF launches leverage the opex base; matures at 46%, well below the 55% CF-only peak (FY2020/22) because five pillars carry more R&D.
base.sbc_rationale: SBC plus withholding at 8.8% of revenue (FY2025 actual), easing ~0.2pp/yr to 7.5%. Withholding scales with the share price, not revenue, so the path is held high.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 3.6%, H1-2026 3.9% (cell-therapy and Boston manufacturing build). Tapers to 3.0%, above the 2.0-2.7% of FY2022-24.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 18% in FY2026 (H1 actual ~19%, plus the remaining catch-up deduction for previously capitalised R&D), then the 19.5-20.5% guided non-GAAP ETR rounded to 21% with Pillar Two.
base.wc_rationale: Specialty pharma: receivables and inventory grow with sales, partly offset by accrued rebates. Negative capture of 10% of each revenue increase.

scenario_narratives.base: Trikafta-to-Alyftrek conversion and patient-population growth keep CF compounding mid-single digits through the early 2030s, while the non-CF pillars - Casgevy (center capacity eases slowly), Journavx (payer coverage now ~260M lives), povetacicept in IgAN (approved on the Nov-2026 PDUFA) and Crinetics' Palsonify/atumelnant - add roughly $5-6B of revenue by FY2032. Revenue grows ~10% near term, fading to 2.5% by FY2035. Margins dip in FY2027 on a full year of Crinetics losses, then recover to 46% pre-SBC as Crinetics turns accretive in 2029. Terminal value is capped at 16x because CF exclusivity (Trikafta ~2037, Alyftrek later) falls just beyond the explicit horizon.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vertex becomes a genuinely diversified rare-disease company: povetacicept extends from IgAN into other B-cell renal diseases, zimislecel is filed and approved as a functional cure for type 1 diabetes, Journavx wins broad acute-pain formulary access and a painful-diabetic-neuropathy label, and Crinetics reaches its >$5B combined peak. Revenue grows 10-12% through FY2031. Operating leverage lifts pre-SBC margins to 50%, and Alyftrek's later patents plus the new pillars justify a 20x exit with 3% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: CF concentration bites. Compulsory-licensing and generic-access campaigns (South Africa, Brazil, India, Ukraine; Beximco's discounted generic) plus US MFN/IRA pricing erode CF net price. AbbVie's TMEM16A or Sionna's mechanisms take share in the 2030s. Casgevy stays bottlenecked, Journavx is boxed in by cheap generics, and povetacicept or zimislecel stumble. The ~$10B Crinetics bet underdelivers on acromegaly/CAH. Growth slows to low single digits by FY2030 and turns negative as the Trikafta LOE approaches. Pre-SBC margins hold near 40% and then compress, and the post-LOE terminal is worth 10x with zero growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: ~85% of revenue is one franchise facing persistent pricing/generic-access pressure and an exclusivity cliff just beyond the horizon, and the company has just committed ~$10B to an unproven endocrine franchise. Base at 50% because FY2026 guidance was raised and H1 execution is on track. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent binary outcomes (zimislecel approval, povetacicept label expansion, Journavx PDN, Crinetics peak sales) to land together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis expenses SBC and the cash tax on net-share settlement (~9% of revenue at Vertex) and strips the ~$0.5B of interest income earned on the cash pile, which the bridge adds back separately. On that basis Vertex is a high-quality but terminal-constrained annuity: most of the value sits in the CF franchise, whose exclusivity ends 1-4 years after the explicit horizon. The street basis treats SBC as non-cash and shows how much of today's price depends on that convention.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple: CF exclusivity (Trikafta ~2037) falls just beyond FY2035. Each turn of cap multiple is worth ~$11/share in the base case (PV of terminal 45.2B at 16x). The price sits above even the street-basis weighted value (band position >100%), so the market is paying for CF durability past 2037 and pipeline success beyond the bull case at an 8% discount rate.
SBC treatment: SBC plus equity-award withholding is ~$1.1B/yr. The house/street band is wide.
Crinetics bridge is an estimate (~$10B less ~$1.15B acquired cash); replace with the Q3-2026 10-Q purchase-price allocation.
Pipeline binaries (povetacicept PDUFA 30-Nov-2026, zimislecel filing) move the bull/base boundary.
CF pricing/generic-access pressure and US drug-pricing policy (MFN, IRA).
